note: Receiver labels are reused across hardware changes: reports and corpus entries before and after a swap both say 'lnb-c'. These boundaries are the only way to separate them. Split on capture start time, not on label. A boundary can move a receiver on a radio nobody touched: pluto-5d4d.lnb-a jumped +566 kHz across the pluto-19f2 swap window, which was recorded here as leaving 5d4d valid. Split on capture start time for every radio, not only the one that was worked on.

measured.survey_active_basis: 351 probes / 2808 tunings per receiver over 23.5 h before the swap

epochs.fault: lnb-c detected 3.3x less often than lnb-d. Its +430 kHz LO offset costs only ~10% of survey score (the survey spans +/-700 kHz centred on zero and does not use receiver_centers), so the offset does not explain the deficit. The unit had a separate hardware fault.

epochs.hardware_note: Both units replaced at once and are identical to each other. Identical model does not imply identical LO: free-running crystals, no shared 10 MHz reference in the chain, so the two offsets are independent draws.
epochs.pending: absolute offsets unknown; measure with lo_sweep once ~40 post-swap corpus probes exist, then write measured_centers_hz

measured.source: lnb_calibration estimator, narrow reports, sweep-clustered bootstrap

epochs.note: lnb-a sat near zero and fired at a median -130.5 kHz, indistinguishable from lnb-b. The recorded receiver_centers_hz of +1,170 Hz was CORRECT for this epoch.

measured.source: survey path, coarse bank E (+/-700 kHz about raw zero), refined points where both ports fired

epochs.fault: lnb-a's LO moved about +566 kHz across the same window that brackets pluto-19f2's LNB swap, even though 5d4d was believed untouched. Its fire rate stepped 8.26% -> 0.24% while lnb-b was unchanged at 6.49% -> 6.87%, and its surviving detections pinned at +349.8 kHz, the search-grid edge. This single event produced BOTH the 'flat ~1.19 peak-to-median, dead port' exclusion in cross_radio.DEAD_RECEIVERS AND the stale receiver_centers_hz. They are one fault, not two: the port was never dead, it moved out of the search.
epochs.why_it_cannot_self_heal: acquisition.py builds frequency_offsets = arange(-350_000, 350_001, 25_000) + centre, where centre is the ALREADY APPLIED receiver_centers value. A port anchored near zero is blind past about +/-356 kHz and can never discover that it has moved. pluto-19f2's replacement LNB was findable only because its stale +434 kHz calibration had already displaced its grid into range. The daily timer will keep returning ~0 Hz for this port forever; the value must be written as measured_centers_hz from the survey path.
epochs.action: set measured_centers_hz: [567402.0, 0.0] for pluto-5d4d; receiver_centers() already prefers that field. Verified: with it applied, lnb-a's signed live window moves from +250..+550 kHz to -300..0 kHz, centroid -158.4 kHz against lnb-b -151.8, lnb-c -155.0, lnb-d -144.1, and the paired per-instant residual is 0.000 kHz, CI [-61, +153] Hz.
